newsitem.title: JAPAN: Kyushu Elec reactor starts commercial operations.
newsitem.headline: Kyushu Elec reactor starts commercial operations.

text.p: Kyushu Electric Power Co Inc's sixth nuclear reactor at its Genkai power plant began commercial operations on Friday morning, the last nuclear reactor to do so this century in Japan.
"We received final approval for commercial operations from the government at 11 a.m. (0200 GMT)," a company spokesman said.

With the new 1.18 million kilowatt (kw) unit operational, 47 percent of Kyushu Electric's electricity is produced by nuclear reactors, while 42 percent is from thermal power plants, nine percent from hydroelectric generators and two percent from geothermal plants.
The electric utility currently has no specific plans to build another reactor, but it intends to add new units to its existing six reactors in the future to meet growing demand, the spokesman said.
The next reactor in Japan -- the 825,000 kw unit at Tohoku Electric Power Co Inc's Onagawa power plant in northern Japan -- is scheduled to be put on the power grid in January 2002.
